prompt: On an AMD machine, `cpuid` leaf 0 returns `ebx = 0x68747541`, `edx = 0x69746E65`, `ecx = 0x444D4163`. Then you read EFER with `rdmsr` and get `edx = 0x1`, `eax = 0x500`. Work out what the kernel sees.

trace.label: [vendor string] after `memcpy`ing ebx, edx, ecx in that order
[mask] to test long-mode support in `edx` of leaf `0x80000001` (bit 29)
EFER = 0x500 has bits 8 and 10 set. What does that say about long mode?

explain: Each register holds four ASCII bytes in little-endian order, so 0x68747541 is 41 75 74 68 = "Auth". The three registers spell the vendor in the order ebx, edx, ecx. Long mode support is edx bit 29 of leaf 0x80000001 (1 << 29 = 0x20000000); bit 20 is NX. `rdmsr` splits the value over edx:eax, so you shift edx up by 32 and OR in eax; without the cast the shift would overflow 32 bits. In EFER, bit 8 (LME) is set by the kernel and bit 10 (LMA) is set by the CPU once paging is also on, so 0x500 means both.
